Each body's force sum\n// still accumulates over j in ascending order, so results are bitwise identical\n// to the scalar formulation; the block lanes are independent and vectorize.\nconstexpr size_t FORCE_BLOCK = 8;\n\nvoid computeForces(std::vector<Body>& bodies) {\n    const size_t n = bodies.size();\n\n    // Structure-of-arrays snapshot of positions (positions are not modified here).\n    std::vector<double> px(n), py(n), pz(n);\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n        px[j] = bodies[j].pos.x;\n        py[j] = bodies[j].pos.y;\n        pz[j] = bodies[j].pos.z;\n    }\n\n    const size_t nBlocked = n - (n % FORCE_BLOCK);\n\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t ib = 0; ib < nBlocked; ib += FORCE_BLOCK) {\n        double xi[FORCE_BLOCK], yi[FORCE_BLOCK], zi[FORCE_BLOCK];\n        double Fx[FORCE_BLOCK] = {}, Fy[FORCE_BLOCK] = {}, Fz[FORCE_BLOCK] = {};\n        for (size_t k = 0; k < FORCE_BLOCK; ++k) {\n            xi[k] = px[ib + k];\n            yi[k] = py[ib + k];\n            zi[k] = pz[ib + k];\n        }\n\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            const double xj = px[j], yj = py[j], zj = pz[j];\n            for (size_t k = 0;
